plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is grown worldwide for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America (native), cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and Asia
plants.funFact: Young sunflowers show heliotropism, following the sun from east to west each day, but mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking July to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region native; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial that rises from muddy water with large, round, water-repellent leaves and stunning, fragrant flowers. It is deeply symbolic in Hinduism and Buddhism and is widely grown in ponds.
plants.location: Asia, including India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and northern Australia; cultivated in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that sheds water and dirt, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low, evergreen shrub that carpets moorlands and heathlands with masses of tiny bell-shaped flowers. It tolerates poor, acidic soils and provides important nectar for bees late in summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, beginning in August
plants.location: Scottish Highlands, Ireland, Scandinavia, and moorlands across Europe and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its gel-like texture and strong flavor, and heather was historically used for thatching, bedding, and brewing ale.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree with feathery foliage that bursts into fragrant golden pom-pom flowers during the southern winter and early spring. It is Australia's national floral emblem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, beginning around July to August
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the green and gold of the wattle inspired the country's national sporting colors.
